comments.body:
> **Dana** · reviewer · owns the eval harness

The step-4 write-up is the reason to read this submission, and I want to make the general form explicit because it is worth more than the capstone.

**An exactly zero delta is data, not a null.** Most people see `+0.0000` and report "no effect". You instrumented it and found that decomposition *did* change the candidate pool for 47 of 60 questions and changed the packed context for **one**. Those are completely different findings:

- "no effect" → the technique does not work
- "the pool changed and the ranking did not" → **the technique works and is redundant with something already in the pipeline**

The second is actionable and the first is not. On a corpus where N=100 does not already contain the second hop, decomposition would earn its keep — and you now know the diagnostic that would tell you.

replies.body:
> **the original poster** · cohort

The thing that nearly stopped me digging was that `+0.0000` looks like a bug, and my first instinct was to check whether the routing was firing at all. It was firing on all 60.

The counter I would give anyone repeating this: **instrument the intermediate stage before you conclude anything about the final metric.** `candidate pool changed: 47` took ten minutes and turned a non-result into the most interesting row in the table.

comments.body:
> **Marcus** · cohort peer

Question about step 2 rather than step 4 — `+0.2500` with a CI of `[+0.182, +0.318]` is enormous. Larger than every other step combined, by a lot.

Is that not suspicious? A single fusion change nearly doubling full-chain recall makes me wonder whether the baseline was straw.

replies.body:
> **Rafael** · cohort peer · came from search infra

Right to be suspicious of a huge delta, and in this case the baseline genuinely is weak — deliberately.

Step 1 is `fixed` chunking, **dense only**, `k=5`. Dense-only on this corpus is the weakest configuration available: the LSA encoder is intentionally modest, and the corpus has a lot of rare identifiers and entity names that lexical matching handles far better than a small dense model does. So step 2 is not really "fusion helped by 0.25" — it is **"adding a lexical leg to a dense-only system helped by 0.25"**, which is a much more specific and much less surprising claim.

That is not a straw baseline, it is a *starting* baseline, and the brief asks for exactly that. But Marcus is right that the row is mislabelled: `+ weighted hybrid α=0.2` describes the change to the config, not the change to the system. **`+ lexical leg (BM25), fused at α=0.2`** is the honest row label, and it makes the size of the delta stop looking suspicious.

> **the original poster** · cohort

Relabelling. That is a fair catch — the row named the parameter I changed rather than the capability I added, and those are not the same thing when the parameter is what switches the capability on.
